biography.plain_text: Lukas Lundin was a Swedish-Canadian mining entrepreneur based in Geneva. He inherited his father's resources business and helped expand it across several continents. A petroleum engineering graduate of New Mexico Tech, he co-founded Lundin Mining with Adolf Lundin and guided its transformation from an exploration company into a substantial copper producer.

confidence.reason: Primary sources establish education and the founding and expansion of Lundin Mining; Bloomberg directly supports inheritance and Swedish-Canadian identity. Geneva is consistent with the established source record and independent biography.

long_biography.plain_text:
Lukas Lundin founded Lundin Gold around an Ecuadorian deposit that many miners considered too difficult to develop. As chairman, he oversaw Fruta del Norte's progression from acquisition to production within five years. The venture reflected his preference for large deposits and teams with the technical experience to turn them into working mines.

His first major mining breakthrough had come in Argentina, where he secured the Bajo de la Alumbrera copper and gold deposit through International Musto. The project culminated in the company's sale to Rio Algom and North Limited. He subsequently co-founded Lucara Diamond with Eira Thomas and Catherine McLeod-Seltzer, financially backing the acquisition and development of Botswana's Karowe mine. Production there began in 2012, followed by plans to extend mining underground.
